analysis.one_liner: BSE Ltd runs India's oldest stock exchange, earning fees on equity and derivatives trading, new company listings, and market data/technology services.
analysis.whats_happening: Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026) results, reported in August 2026, showed net profit of ~Rs 873 crore, up 62% year-on-year, on record revenue of ~Rs 1,707 crore (+63% YoY), driven mainly by derivatives trading income. Q2 FY27 results are due around 4 November 2026, about three weeks away. In mid-October 2026 the stock rose roughly 2-3% after a SEBI advisory panel reportedly favoured retaining the existing 30-minute VWAP method for derivatives settlement over a proposed Closing Auction Session-linked formula, easing fears of a hit to BSE's high-margin options business.
analysis.plain_terms: BSE is the exchange where Indian investors buy and sell shares, and it earns a small fee on every trade, listing, and data service it provides. Its profit has roughly tripled over two years mainly because trading in weekly index options surged after regulators forced NSE and BSE onto separate expiry days in September 2025, pushing volume toward BSE. That is the tension to hold onto: this growth engine is largely a function of where SEBI currently sets the rules, not pure organic demand. If SEBI curbs weekly options or changes settlement mechanics, as it is actively debating now, the revenue line BSE depends on most could shrink quickly.
analysis.quarters: Profit has risen for five straight quarters: Q1FY26 ~Rs 539cr, Q2FY26 ~Rs 558cr, Q3FY26 ~Rs 602cr, Q4FY26 ~Rs 797cr, Q1FY27 ~Rs 873cr. Q1FY27 revenue of ~Rs 1,707cr was up 63% YoY, with EBITDA margin expanding to about 67% from 65% a year earlier. Management attributed the growth to 'higher transaction-related income, especially from derivatives, robust listing activity, and growing colocation services.' Full FY26 profit was ~Rs 2,487cr, up 88% YoY - a real and large number, but one substantially driven by the September 2025 NSE/BSE expiry-day split rather than market-wide volume growth, so treat the growth rate as partly structural/regulatory rather than purely organic.
analysis.performance_read: Over 5 years the split-adjusted stock is up roughly 2,153% versus the Nifty's 25% - an extraordinary run. However, the current price of Rs 3,363 sits 23.4% below the Rs 4,391.73 peak hit on 26 May 2026, around the time of the Q4FY26 results. Two 3:1 stock splits (March 2022 and May 2025) multiplied the share count ninefold since listing; the return and price figures here are already split-adjusted, so the 23.4% drawdown is a genuine price fall, not a corporate-action artifact. Over the last year and the last 3 months, peer MCX has outpaced BSE (70% vs 34% over 1Y; +15% vs -6% over 3M), suggesting the market currently prefers MCX's commodity-derivatives story to BSE's.
analysis.valuation_read: At a TTM P/E of roughly 49x and P/B of roughly 15.5x (not independently cross-verified - treat as approximate), BSE trades well above the market average, which is normal for a debt-free exchange with very high incremental margins. It is expensive because profit has roughly tripled in two years on a derivatives-volume surge; whether that is justified depends entirely on whether BSE's enlarged derivatives market share is structural or a side-effect of SEBI's 2025 expiry-day rule that a future regulatory change could partly reverse. One other source quoted a trailing P/E near 70x around the May 2026 peak - the gap with the 49x figure likely reflects earnings catching up with price and the price itself falling since then, rather than a contradiction.
analysis.growth_read: Growth has been overwhelmingly volume-led, not margin-led: EBITDA margin moved only from about 65% to 67% YoY, a modest shift next to the 63% revenue jump, meaning most of the profit increase came from a jump in trading activity rather than pricing power or cost discipline. That trading-volume jump itself traces largely to the September 2025 Tuesday/Thursday expiry-day split between NSE and BSE. Listing income (97 new equity listings in a recent quarter, raising Rs 53,548 crore) and colocation/data revenue form a smaller, steadier layer underneath the derivatives-driven swings.
analysis.health_read: BSE is debt-free with ROE of about 37% and ROCE of about 49%; as a fee-based, asset-light exchange operator its accounting profit converts into cash readily, with no working-capital or receivables concern. The risk here is not financial (no leverage, no promoter pledging since there is no promoter) but business/regulatory risk: a large share of current profit depends on derivatives rules that SEBI can alter by circular, as illustrated by the stock's reaction to the October 2026 SEBI panel debate over settlement mechanics.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters hold 0% of BSE - it has been a demutualised, professionally run exchange with no promoter group since listing, so there is no pledging to track. Shareholding splits roughly between the public (around 54%), domestic institutions (around 24%), and foreign institutions (estimates ranged 21-28% across sources and were not fully reconciled). We found no evidence in available 2026 shareholding data that Rakesh Jhunjhunwala/Rare Enterprises (now run by Rekha Jhunjhunwala) currently holds a stake in BSE - if that association exists in a reader's memory, it is not confirmed here, so it should be treated as unverified rather than assumed true.
strengths: Five consecutive quarters of profit growth, from ~Rs 539cr (Q1FY26) to ~Rs 873cr (Q1FY27)
Zero debt, with ROE of ~37% and ROCE of ~49%
EBITDA margin expanded to ~67% in Q1FY27 from ~65% a year earlier, showing operating leverage
Strong listing franchise: 97 new equity listings in a recent quarter, raising Rs 53,548 crore
watchpoints: Stock down 23.4% from its 26 May 2026 peak of Rs 4,391.73, a fall that lines up with the Q4FY26 results period
TTM P/E of ~49x prices in continued derivatives growth, but FY26's 88% profit growth was partly a one-off benefit of the September 2025 NSE/BSE expiry-day split rather than organic demand

SEBI is actively reconsidering derivatives settlement mechanics (CAS vs VWAP) and has signalled a preference for longer-tenure contracts over weekly expiries - either change could cut into BSE's most profitable revenue line
NSE's own CEO said on 25 September 2026 that market share is 'returning' to NSE in equity options, suggesting BSE's derivatives share gain may not be permanent
analysis.one_thing: SEBI's eventual decision on derivatives settlement mechanics (the CAS vs VWAP debate) and on weekly versus longer-tenure expiry contracts - this determines whether BSE's current derivatives-driven profit surge is structural or temporary.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked recent quarterly profit figures (~Rs 873cr, 797cr, 602cr, 558cr, 539cr) across Kotak Securities, Angel One, Business Standard and Trendlyne, which were broadly consistent. P/E (~49.55x) and P/B (~15.5x) came from a single aggregator and were not independently cross-verified; one other source quoted a ~70x trailing P/E near the May 2026 peak, likely an earlier, pre-earnings-growth snapshot rather than a genuine contradiction. FII shareholding percentage varied across sources (21% to 28%) and was not fully reconciled. Could not verify whether any specific marquee investor currently holds a stake in BSE - this absence is reported as unverified, not as a confirmed negative.
